hook: It took 8 years and 6 billion miles to reach Mercury.

sections.voiceover: It took 8 years and 6 billion miles to reach Mercury.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic 3D render of the sun scorching the barren, cratered surface of Mercury with a tiny spacecraft silhouette approaching in the distance.
sections.sfx_cue: Deep sub-bass drone rising into solar wind whistle
b_roll: ESA digital animation of BepiColombo approaching Mercury
Close-up render of solar panels reflecting blinding sunlight

sections.voiceover: In November 2026, the BepiColombo spacecraft enters orbit around Mercury. Built by the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, it carries two orbiters. What will it find beneath Mercury's surface?
sections.visual_cue: Detailed breakdown diagram showing the combined BepiColombo spacecraft separating into two distinct orbiter modules.
sections.sfx_cue: Mechanical locking hum followed by low orchestral swell
b_roll: Cleanroom assembly footage of ESA Mercury Planetary Orbiter
JAXA launch preparation footage of Mio orbiter

sections.voiceover: Only one probe, NASA's MESSENGER, has ever orbited this planet before.
sections.visual_cue: Archival trajectory map showing NASA's MESSENGER probe circling the innermost planet against dark space.
sections.sfx_cue: Static radio chime with heartbeat pulse
b_roll: High-contrast radar mapping flyover of Mercury craters

sections.voiceover: Between 2011 and 2015, MESSENGER revealed unexpected geological activity. Now, the Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Mio orbiter will examine those secrets. Together they mark only the 2nd mission in history to orbit Mercury.
sections.visual_cue: Split-screen visualization showcasing MESSENGER thermal survey maps alongside 3D scans of sub-surface geological structures.
sections.sfx_cue: Resonant metallic pulse expanding into atmospheric synth synth drop
b_roll: NASA MESSENGER false-color geological surface imagery
ESA simulation of Mercury Planetary Orbiter mapping instruments

sections.voiceover: BepiColombo's entering orbit around Mercury in November 2026 to uncover its hidden geology.
sections.visual_cue: Wide cinematic shot of the spacecraft floating in silent orbit with the massive bright limb of the sun crowning behind Mercury.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft resolving orchestral chime fading out
b_roll: High-resolution photographic horizon render of Mercury
Spacecraft solar array silhouette against solar glare
